access_evidence: GET /api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages?stages=award&limit=100 returned HTTP 200 three times (~1.1 MB each), 300 award-stage releases, 316 KB-1.1 MB each, containing awards[].suppliers[].name.
blockers: NO_CPV_OR_KEYWORD_FILTER: HTTP 400 'Request parameter keyword is not recognised, allowed parameters are: stages, limit, cursor, updatedFrom, updatedTo'. Medical awards must be found by scanning.
NO_AWARD_DATE: awards[] carries no date; release.date is the publication date, so event_at is null unless contracts[].dateSigned exists.
NO_FIXED_SAMPLE_WINDOW: the 'most recent award releases' window is not a calendar period, so only the medical share of the sample generalises.
historical_depth: not verified (the API is a rolling updatedFrom/updatedTo window)
licence_note: The OCDS package declares its own licence field: 'http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/' (read verbatim from DATASETS/industry/uk_find_a_tender/raw/award_packages_p1.json). Open Government Licence v3.0.
name: UK Find a Tender Service — OCDS release packages
notes: Supplier identity is CONFIRMED only when the buyer published a legal identifier (10 of 62 rows).
operator: UK Cabinet Office / Crown Commercial Service
rate_policy: No key, no documented quota; the API rejects unknown parameters (HTTP 400) and accepts only stages, limit, cursor, updatedFrom, updatedTo.
unlock_route: No access blocker. For a census, page with cursor / updatedFrom; the only real limitation is the absence of a server-side subject filter.
what_is_new: 62 UK award-supplier rows for medical CPV codes, from a scan of 300 award-stage releases (16 medical releases, 32 medical awards, 100% with a named supplier). Establishes that UK FTS *does* expose award suppliers, unlike TED's legacy notices.
